rationale:
Evidence: every design so far ended off-track in all 60 trials, with max_error stuck at about 0.061 to 0.066 m against a 0.06 m limit. rms_error stayed near 0.03 m whatever the gain. Halving the weights (iteration 1) and cutting kp from 3 to 1.2 (iteration 3) changed progress only a little, so gain is not the limiting factor. The common failure is an excursion to the edge of the allowed band, with 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. Line loss is likely at the edge, when the outer sensors reach the end of their reach and throttle drops to 0.35.

Changes: (1) Widen the sensor array to x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 (was +/-0.032). The outer sensors then still see the tape at larger lateral offsets, which should reduce line-loss events at the edge. (2) Move sensors to y = 0.06 so the steering reacts slightly earlier. (3) Keep weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1] so the signal scale stays the same as the best run. (4) Raise base_speed to 1.0 from 0.9 to move progress up, since the wider array should give more margin. (5) kp 1.6 sits between the over-steered runs and the slow iteration 3 run. ki 0.5 targets the constant motor-mismatch bias, and kd 1.2 damps the faster response. (6) Keep mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.14, wheel_radius 0.03 and line_loss last_direction, so the sensor-span and gain changes can be read from the race.

Expected result: fewer line-loss events, max_error under about 0.05 m, and progress above the 0.17 best seen so far on the oval. Completion within 3 s is still unlikely at this speed. Uncertainty: the cause of the consistent 0.06 m excursion is not confirmed, so this is a diagnostic step as well as an improvement attempt.
